title: Normalization of the global boundary of the pro-etale support triangle
statement:
Fix a finite commutative ring $A$. Let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be a closed immersion of schemes with quasi-compact complementary open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Work with ordinary constant-$A$ module sheaves on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules] and their derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with exact $i_*$ and $i^*,j^*$ as in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Put $i^!_0M=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$ [def-pur-flasque-support], and write $S=Ri^!_0$ on $D^+$, with its support counit $\epsilon:i_*SK\to K$ as in [lem-pur-support-localization-triangle]. Let $K\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, represented by a bounded-below complex of injective module sheaves $I$. Let $\beta:Rj_*j^*K\to(i_*SK)[1]$ be the third arrow of the support triangle constructed from this injective resolution with the cone convention [def-pur-support-triangle, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Derived global sections identify that entire triangle with
$$R\Gamma_Z(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,j^*K)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_Z(X,K)[1],$$
where the first term is identified by the sectionwise support kernel and the third by the direct-image/sections comparison. More precisely, the sequence of complexes of $A$-modules
$$0\to\Gamma_Z(X,I)\to I(X)\to(j^*I)(U)\to0$$
is degreewise short exact, $j^*I$ computes $j^*K$, and its usual cochain connecting homomorphism equals $H^q(R\Gamma(X,\beta))$ under these identifications. For every $q\in\mathbf Z$, a cocycle $c\in(j^*I)^q(U)$ and a lift $b\in I^q(X)$, that homomorphism sends $[c]$ to $[db]\in H^{q+1}(\Gamma_Z(X,I))$. Thus it is precisely the supported-cohomology boundary $\partial$ of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness], with no extra sign. These identifications and the boundary are natural in $K$.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal E=i_*i^!_0I$, $\mathcal B=I$, and $\mathcal C=j_*j^*I$. The supported-kernel comparison identifies $\mathcal E$ with $\ker(\mathcal B\to\mathcal C)$, and the injective support exactness lemma gives $0\to\mathcal E\xrightarrow{u}\mathcal B\xrightarrow{v}\mathcal C\to0$ degreewise. The first map is the kernel inclusion under this comparison, not an arbitrarily scaled map. The support localization theorem identifies its associated cone triangle with the triangle of the statement, with first arrow the support counit and second arrow the open unit.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence and first distinguished triangle; pro-etale module specialization using cited ringed-site results

proof.text: The ringed open-closed lemma supplies the exact left adjoint $j_!$ of $j^*$. Thus $j^*I$ is termwise injective by the right-adjoint injectivity lemma. Exactness of $j^*$ shows that it represents $j^*K$. Both $i_*$ and $j_*$ preserve injectives by the same lemma, since their left adjoints $i^*,j^*$ are exact. The injective support global model says that $i^!_0I$ is termwise injective and represents $SK$. Therefore $\mathcal E,\mathcal B,\mathcal C$ are bounded-below complexes of injectives on $X$. The derived-unit comparisons for such complexes compute $R\Gamma(X,-)$ by ordinary sections; they compute $R\Gamma(U,j^*K)$ by $\Gamma(U,j^*I)$ and $R\Gamma_Z(X,K)$ by $\Gamma_Z(X,I)$.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence and first distinguished triangle; pro-etale module specialization using cited ringed-site results

proof.text: On the chosen small model of the pro-etale site, the complementary open $U\to X$ is a monomorphism into the terminal object. Apply the ringed-site injective restriction lemma to each $I^r$, with the constant ring sheaf $A_X$: $I^r(X)\to I^r(U)$ is surjective. This uses injectivity as an $A_X$-module, without asserting injectivity of the underlying abelian sheaf. Set $E=\Gamma_Z(X,I)$, $F=I(X)$, and $G=\Gamma(U,j^*I)$. Sections preserve the kernel in step 1, so $0\to E\xrightarrow{u_X}F\xrightarrow{v_X}G\to0$ is degreewise short exact. The equality $\Gamma(X,j_*j^*I)=\Gamma(U,j^*I)$ is the defining section formula for direct image, and identifies $\Gamma(X,v)$ with restriction.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence and first distinguished triangle; pro-etale module specialization using cited ringed-site results

proof.text: Let $P=\operatorname{Cone}(u)$ with the convention of the statement. Its terms $I^r\oplus\mathcal E^{r+1}$ are injective: given a map from a subobject into this finite direct sum, extend each component by injectivity and pair the two extensions. Thus $P$ too is a bounded-below injective complex. The derived-unit comparisons consequently identify $R\Gamma(X,P)$ with $\Gamma(X,P)=\operatorname{Cone}(u_X)$, since sections preserve finite direct sums and the displayed differential matrix. They identify the cone inclusion with the inclusion of $F$ and the third map with $-\operatorname{pr}_E$, including the shift: sections sends the shifted differential $-d$ to $-d$. The first term is $E$ by the sectionwise supported-kernel comparison. Hence these comparisons identify the entire derived-global cone triangle and its first two arrows, not just its three objects.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: The cone-to-quotient lemma applies to the sheaf sequence of step 1 and the module sequence of step 3. Their comparison maps are respectively $q:P\to\mathcal C$, $(b,a)\mapsto v(b)$, and $q_X:\operatorname{Cone}(u_X)\to G$, $(b,a)\mapsto v_X(b)$, and both are quasi-isomorphisms. The derived-unit comparisons are natural for $q$, so $R\Gamma(X,q)$ is identified with $\Gamma(X,q)=q_X$ between the injective models. Inverting these maps identifies the global third arrow with $(-\operatorname{pr}_E)\circ q_X^{-1}:G\to E[1]$. Together with step 4 this gives the asserted identification of the whole support triangle with the global supported-cohomology triangle and the direct-image/sections comparison on its third object.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: Fix any integer $q$ and a cocycle $c\in G^q$. Step 3 gives a lift $b\in F^q$. Since $v_X(db)=dc=0$, there is a unique $a\in E^{q+1}$ with $u_X(a)=db$. Then $u_X(da)=d^2b=0$ and injectivity of $u_X$ gives $da=0$. In the cone, $d(b,-a)=(db-u_X(a),da)=0$ and $q_X(b,-a)=c$. The third arrow is minus projection, so it sends this cocycle to $a$. Thus the induced boundary sends $[c]$ to $[a]=[db]$ under the kernel identification. Both minus signs are necessary: one in $(b,-a)$ and one in the third arrow.

source.place: Tag 014Z, section-canonical-delta-functor, cone-to-quotient construction with third arrow -p composed with inverse(q); definition-cone

proof.text: The result is independent of choices: another lift $b+u_X(t)$ changes $a$ to $a+dt$, and replacing $c$ by $c+dg$ permits the lift $b+dh$ for any lift $h$ of $g$, leaving $a$ unchanged. Addition and $A$-linearity follow by adding and scaling lifts. This is exactly the usual cochain snake construction for the short exact sequence in step 3. The derived injective boundary normalization identifies that snake boundary with the natural derived supported-cohomology boundary, whose long exact sequence is the one in the support exactness theorem. The kernel functor used there is precisely $\Gamma_Z$, so the map just computed is $\partial$ with no sign change.

source.place: Tag 09XP, section-cohomology-support, injective restriction sequence and first distinguished triangle; pro-etale module specialization using cited ringed-site results

proof.text: For a chain map $f:I\to I\prime$, restriction and the kernel inclusion give a morphism of the short exact sequences of steps 1 and 3. On cones it is $(b,a)\mapsto(fb,fa)$; this commutes with $q_X$ and minus projection. On cocycles, $fb$ lifts $fc$ and $d(fb)=f(db)$, giving the boundary square explicitly; the general long-exact-sequence naturality lemma gives the same square. Finally each bounded-below injective complex is K-injective, and morphisms into a K-injective are computed in the homotopy category. Thus every derived morphism between the represented objects is given by such a chain map, uniquely up to homotopy. All additive functors here carry a homotopy to its termwise image, so the comparisons and squares are independent of that representative and natural in $K$, including comparison between two injective resolutions.
